description: Behavior evals — does the orchestrator run test-first (RED before implementation), split a large task into disjoint-ownership parallel lanes (single lane otherwise), integrate + review the merged result, cap retries, and stop at approved review by offering git-ship rather than pushing?

evals.name: tdd-order-red-before-green
evals.prompt: Build task F01-T02 (validate login form fields) from the backlog.
evals.expected_output: The tester is dispatched first in tdd-red mode and returns 🔴 red-confirmed (tests failing on assertions, no implementation); only then is the developer dispatched in tdd-green mode to drive those tests green; then the reviewer reviews. Artifacts land under .pipeline-artifacts/<run-id>/.
files: a repo with backlog/features/01-auth/tasks/*F01-T02*.md and a React app

assertions.text: Tester runs before the developer (tests written before implementation)
Tester returns 🔴 red-confirmed before any implementation exists
Developer is dispatched in tdd-green mode against the tester's failing tests
A review report is produced under .pipeline-artifacts/<run-id>/review-report.md

evals.name: parallel-lanes-disjoint-ownership
evals.prompt: Build the auth module task: it covers a login form, a session store, and password reset.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator plans multiple lanes with non-overlapping owned paths (e.g. login / session / reset), defines shared interfaces up front, runs each lane's tester→developer concurrently in its own worktree, then merges (conflict-free) and does one review. A task that can't be split cleanly falls back to a single lane.
files: a repo whose auth work spans clearly separable directories

assertions.text: plan.md defines lanes with non-overlapping owned file sets
Shared interfaces/types are defined before lanes fan out
One review runs over the merged result, not one per lane
Worktrees are cleaned up on completion

evals.name: stops-at-review-offers-ship
evals.prompt: Develop and test this: add a footer newsletter signup, then we're done.
evals.expected_output: On an approved review the orchestrator writes pipeline-summary.md, flips the backlog task status to done only if the task came from backlog/, and OFFERS /git-ship — it does not push, commit to a remote, or open a PR on its own.

assertions.text: Does not push or open a PR automatically
Writes pipeline-summary.md with the run-id and artifact paths
